intro: A folk duo from New York's Lower East Side, formed in 1963.
story: Peter Stampfel, on fiddle and banjo, and the guitarist Steve Weber formed the Holy Modal Rounders in 1963, and their rewrite of Hesitation Blues on that first Prestige record is credited as the first song to use the word psychedelic in popular music. Rounder Records took its name from them. They played Pickathon in 1999, the year Rounder released Too Much Fun!, their first album in more than two decades, which Robert Christgau graded an A. The original pair played together for the last time in 2002, a documentary called Bound to Lose followed in 2006, and Weber died on February 7, 2020. Stampfel, at 86, released his solo album Song Shards on Jalopy in 2025.

intro: A Portland country singer and her longtime duo partner.
story: Susannah Weaver got the name Little Sue in college, where her friend was Big Sue, and she kept it as her stage name while teaching school. Willamette Week called her arguably the Portland face of late-1990s alt-country, and she has opened for Roger McGuinn and Loudon Wainwright III. Her album New Light, in 2013, was produced by Mike Coykendall with Jenny Conlee of the Decemberists among the players.

intro: A flute and banjo player who was about to lead Solas.
story: Seamus Egan, whose name the lineup spells Eagan, was born in Hatboro, Pennsylvania, to Irish parents, and the family moved to County Mayo when he was three. By 14 he had won All-Ireland championships on four instruments. Back in the United States from 1980, he took banjo lessons from Mick Moloney in Philadelphia. His band Solas played its first show in Washington, D.C., in 1995, and its second album, Sunny Spells and Scattered Showers, won rave reviews in 1997. Egan toured in 2018 as the Seamus Egan Project, a return to the early days of Solas.
